newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks eke out modest gains by close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks eke out modest gains by close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2654 +9 US 30yr cl 6.55 steady
10yrbond futs 93.350 +0.080 Gold NY 318.25 Lon fix 319.75
*Stocks garner light gains by close but trade patchy and mixed, turnover very quiet. Vol 232.73 million, value A$495.49 million, 1,079 stocks traded, 299 steady, 395 up, 385 down.
The Australian share market eked out some modest gains after a patchy performance by the close on Wednesday with only minimal interest shown by investors.
The All Ordinaries index added 8.8 points to 2,646.4, while September share price index futures contracts were nine points higher at 2,654, a 7.6 point premium to the underlying index.

Turnover struggled to top the A$500 million mark, a clear indication of the abject lack of investor interest, with brokers saying offshore traders were turned away by concerns over the rapidly declining Australian dollar.
"Volumes were slight, probably because of the Australian dollar. It is always a big factor in overseas traders' minds," said a Sydney-based broker.
Trade was mixed with a short term view reflected in the choppy trading conditions.
"It was all over the place. BHP ran hard then fell away and the banks were a bit mixed," the broker said.
Bellwether BHP ended down eight at A$18.19 in volatile trade, while among banks, Commonwealth Bank added 17 cents to A$16.33, while Westpac Banking Corp made most ground, up 13 cents to A$7.80.
"Some people may be more confident on the Bank of Melbourne (bid) but it was probably more just trading factors on the day," the broker said.

The market is waiting for the Australian Competition and Consumer Commision's ruling on Westpac's A$9.75 a share bid for the Victorian-based Bank of Melbourne. Bank of Melbourne shares closed 3.5 cents higher at A$9.43.

In the recently beleaguered gold sector takeover speculation around Joseph Gutnick-controlled Great Central Mines Ltd stole the show as rumours did the rounds of a possible bid from giant Canadian gold miner Barrick Gold.
Great Central shares jumped 10 percent to A$2.71 by the close, although the company denied a bid was on the table or that it was aware of any such bid.
"The talk is in the market. It is probably a 50/50 bet," said Peter Morgan, Australian equities manager at Perpetual Funds Management.

Toll road operator Hills Motorway fell 5.7 percent to A$1.98 amid concerns its M2 motorway in Sydney was not meeting expectations. The company said that while it may restructure the toll, it was too early to tell if the motorway, opened in June, was performing above or below expectations.
Retailer Coles Myer turned in a solid performance, up 24 cents to A$6.70, although traders said it was recovering some of its recent lost ground rather than reacting to news.
"It lost a lot of ground in the last couple of days and it just a recovery of that on fairly light turnover," Perpetual's Morgan said.
Rises barely shaded falls, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
Futures trade slowed from the hectic business of the last two days with 5,683 September SPI contracts traded.
Options trade was moderate with just 31,068 options traded.

In other local markets, Australian bonds rallied amid a technical short squeeze, although the outlook for official interest rates is becoming somewhat clouded by the sustained weakness in the local dollar.
By 5.00 p.m.(0700 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 6.67 pct, down from Tuesday's 6.75.

The Australian dollar slumped to its lowest local close in two years as dealers found new reasons to be bearish at every turn. By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), the dollar had extended an offshore rout to cower at US$0.7332/37 having started at US$0.7345/50 from US$0.7360/65 late here on Tuesday.
